paragraphs.text: Almost everyone puts off tasks they should do, but researchers explain the habit in different ways. Dr Helen Park argues that procrastination is not a problem of laziness but of emotion: people delay tasks that make them feel anxious or bored, in order to feel better in the short term.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Economist James Reid focuses on how people value time. His research suggests that rewards in the future feel smaller than rewards today, so people choose a pleasant activity now even when they know a deadline will cause stress later.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Neuroscientist Sofia Almeida has used brain scans to study the habit. She found that people who often procrastinate show stronger activity in a region linked to recognising threats, which may explain why unpleasant tasks feel so hard to begin.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The three researchers disagree about solutions. Park recommends that people first notice the feeling a task causes, while Reid suggests setting small rewards for each step. Almeida is more cautious, saying that brain research cannot yet tell us which strategies work best.
paragraphs.label: D

items.quote: Neuroscientist Sofia Almeida has used brain scans to study the habit
items.prompt: uses images of the brain as evidence

explanation.en: Almeida “has used brain scans” — that is “images of the brain” → C.
explanation.kk: Алмейда «has used brain scans» — ми суреттері, яғни «images of the brain» → C.
explanation.ru: Алмейда «has used brain scans» — снимки мозга и есть «images of the brain» → C.

items.quote: people delay tasks that make them feel anxious or bored, in order to feel better in the short term
items.prompt: says that putting off tasks helps people escape unpleasant feelings

explanation.en: Park: people delay tasks that make them anxious or bored “in order to feel better in the short term” → A.
explanation.kk: Парк: адамдар мазасыздық не жалығу тудыратын тапсырмаларды «in order to feel better in the short term» кейінге қалдырады → A.
explanation.ru: Парк: люди откладывают задачи, от которых им тревожно или скучно, «in order to feel better in the short term» → A.

items.quote: Reid suggests setting small rewards for each step
items.prompt: recommends rewarding progress through a task

explanation.en: “Reid suggests setting small rewards for each step” → B. Park, in the same sentence, recommends something else — noticing the feeling.
explanation.kk: «Reid suggests setting small rewards for each step» → B. Сол сөйлемде Парк басқаны ұсынады — өз сезіміңді байқауды.
explanation.ru: «Reid suggests setting small rewards for each step» → B. Парк в том же предложении советует другое — замечать свои чувства.

items.quote: brain research cannot yet tell us which strategies work best
items.prompt: doubts that current research can show which methods are best

explanation.en: Almeida is cautious: “brain research cannot yet tell us which strategies work best” → C. C appears twice, as the NB allows.
explanation.kk: Алмейда сақ: «brain research cannot yet tell us which strategies work best» → C. C әрпі екінші рет — NB рұқсат береді.
explanation.ru: Алмейда осторожна: «brain research cannot yet tell us which strategies work best» → C. Буква C второй раз — это допускает NB.

items.quote: rewards in the future feel smaller than rewards today
items.prompt: explains the habit through the way people value future benefits
keywords: rewards in the future feel smaller

explanation.en: Reid: “rewards in the future feel smaller than rewards today”, so people choose pleasure now → B.
explanation.kk: Рид: «rewards in the future feel smaller than rewards today», сондықтан адамдар қазіргі рахатты таңдайды → B.
explanation.ru: Рид: «rewards in the future feel smaller than rewards today», поэтому люди выбирают удовольствие сейчас → B.
